text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.66% today after crude oil prices dropped for a second day on hopes for a diplomatic resolution to the Iran conflict. The stock had surged nearly $7 over the prior four trading days as geopolitical tensions pushed oil above $150, but that rally reversed sharply when both U.S. and Iranian leadership signaled openness to negotiation — reducing the risk premium that had been supporting energy prices.

The broader political backdrop adds another headwind: Democrats taking control of Congress signals a potential shift toward renewable energy investment and away from oil-focused policies, which weighs on the outlook for oil majors even as crude prices remain historically elevated at $103 domestically and $123 globally.
